prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: מערכת שעות כיתת י'2 – סמסטר א' (language he, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 6 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "ראשון" spans 1 col × 2 row; "שני" spans 1 col × 2 row; "שלישי" spans 1 col × 3 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "יום" · longest unbreakable word 36px · one-line width 36px
  col 2: header "שעה" · longest unbreakable word 42px · one-line width 78px
  col 3: header "מקצוע" · longest unbreakable word 56px · one-line width 56px
  col 4: header "מורה" · longest unbreakable word 37px · one-line width 60px
  col 5: header "חדר" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 67px
  col 6: header "הערות" · longest unbreakable word 57px · one-line width 619px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 629px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 628px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"A weekly class timetable (grade י'2, semester א') read by day: a reader finds the day, then scans across the lesson block for time, subject, teacher and room, and finally reads the note that qualifies the lesson (homework, group split, room change, cancellation).","reading":"Right-to-left, top-to-bottom. The eye anchors on the merged day label, then runs leftwards through שעה → מקצוע → מורה → חדר, with הערות as an optional trailing annotation. Comparison is mostly vertical within a day (times march down in order) and across days for the same subject/teacher; the room number is the value a reader most often plucks out in isolation.","groups":["יום + שעה — the 'when' pair; the day cell is a merged anchor for 2–3 consecutive rows, so it frames the time column","מקצוע + מורה + חדר — the lesson identity triplet read as one sweep and the core of the scan","הערות — a separate annotation layer, not a peer of the triplet; it is prose, not a short field"],"keep_intact":["time ranges 08:15–09:00 etc. (78px unbreakable — must never break at the dash or wrap)","room values 204/112/305/210/118 and 'מעבדה 1'","teacher names (אבי שפירא, רונית לוי, מיכל אדרי)","subject names (מתמטיקה, תנ\"ך, היסטוריה)","day labels ראשון/שני/שלישי"],"may_wrap":["הערות — long free prose (up to 619px on one line); it may wrap to 2–4 lines and the merged day cell already gives those rows vertical room","header words שעה/מקצוע/מורה/חדר if needed, but only at word boundaries"],"note":"Only the widths are under control; total must stay ≤628px. Because the day column is row-merged, extra height from wrapped notes does not break the row-unit reading — but very long notes will visibly stretch the whole row."}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [57, 99, 77, 81, 88, 226] · table 629×548px · row heights [33, 73, 73, 73, 73, 73, 53, 94] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [60, 110, 80, 85, 93, 200] · table 629×568px · row heights [33, 73, 73, 73, 73, 73, 73, 94] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 4 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [65, 108, 90, 95, 95, 175] · table 629×669px · row heights [33, 94, 94, 94, 73, 94, 73, 114] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 5 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
